rules.title: Source of Income Discrimination Protections (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent to, or treat differently, an applicant or tenant because they pay rent with a housing subsidy such as a Section 8 voucher or other public assistance; 'No Section 8' policies are illegal.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers statewide under the Fair Employment and Housing Act's source of income protections.
rules.quoted_span: “source of income” means lawful, verifiable income paid directly to a tenant, or to a representative of a tenant, or paid to a housing owner or landlord on behalf of a tenant, including federal, state, or local public assistance, and federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including, but not limited to, federal housing assistance vouchers issued under Section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937

rules.title: Criminal History Screening Limitations (FEHA / Civil Rights Council regulations)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests without conviction, sealed/expunged records, or juvenile records, cannot impose blanket bans on applicants with any criminal history, and must show a conviction is directly related to tenant suitability before denying based on it.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all housing providers statewide under California fair housing law regulations on criminal history screening, effective January 1, 2020.
rules.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2, § 12269 (Civil Rights Council regulations)
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.conflict_note: Exact regulatory citation section not stated in source text; attributed based on known 2019 Civil Rights Council regulations effective Jan 1, 2020 described in secondary source P7/P9.
